topic: Part 6.15 Silent-Ignore Cohort — scoreboard records hits but never misses (EXP-606)
change_summary: New subsection 6.15 integrated from EXP-606: 10-entry silent-ignore cohort + author-status standardization (8 PREDs flipped pending->dome_silent_terminal). Deep-attack review.
our_argument_summary: The dome registers falsifiable predictions but only updates its public scoreboard when a prediction is confirmed; expired/failed predictions sit indefinitely as pending, so the win tally is computed over a process that never records a loss. Ten closed windows, zero dome-posted results; our independent column resolves to 7 standard_physics/recycled, 2 tacit_withdrawal, 1 falsified — none dome-discriminating.

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Section is aggregation prose over predictions.json. Verified every cohort row against predictions.json: all 10 our_verdict values match (087/088/111/085/077/081 standard_physics, 090 recycled, 106/105 tacit_withdrawal, 073 falsified); author_status flips to dome_silent_terminal present for the 8 specified PREDs; PRED-073 correctly left dome_silent (8d<14d). Window-close dates and silence-day counts (39/51/8) reproduce exactly as-of 2026-06-08.
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: Silence-day counts are static snapshots as-of 2026-06-08 (today 2026-06-09 -> would be +1). Acceptable for a published section but see minor hole.
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: PRED-073 falsified verdict is explicitly caveated as rule-based-under-consensus-null, not a fresh contradicting measurement.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: None in the per-PRED data. The one inaccuracy is a COMPLETENESS claim, not a data value — see holes_found H1.

holes_found.description: COHORT INCOMPLETENESS contradicts the sections own anti-cherry-picking defense. Section 6.15 states the cohort is “defined mechanically — every prediction whose window has closed with no dome-posted result.” But predictions.json contains 14 closed-window/no-result entries, and two PRED-class entries that match this exact criterion are silently omitted: PRED-072 (TTB +/-15 nT, closed 2026-04-11, pending, our_verdict standard_physics) and PRED-084 (P-wave shadow zone 104-140deg, closed 2026-04-11, pending, standard_physics). Both are already itemized as part of OUR Section 6.12 “eleven April closures” list (PRED-072,077,081,084,085,087,088,090,105,106,111). Section 6.15 re-includes NINE of those eleven, adds the new PRED-073, but drops exactly 072 and 084 — the only two whose close date is 2026-04-11 rather than 2026-04-30. So the operative rule is NOT “every prediction” (nine of 6.12s eleven are re-listed) and NOT “avoid 6.12 overlap” (those nine overlap) — the exclusion of 072/084 is arbitrary and undisclosed. Most charitable read: the analyst built the cohort around the 2026-04-30 closure batch and overlooked the earlier 04-11 pair. Either way the published completeness claim is falsifiable-and-false, and it appears in the ONE section whose entire thesis is that the dome practices selective accounting — a dome defender gets a free “physician, heal thyself” rebuttal. (MT-003 entry_type=manual_test reclassified data_predates_registration, and PROS-003 entry_type=prospective tracked as FAIL-008 in uncounted-failures.json, are both defensibly out of scope; 072/084 are not.)
holes_found.recommendation: Preferred: ADD PRED-072 and PRED-084 to the cohort table as two rows (window close 2026-04-11, 58d silent, dome status pending->dome_silent_terminal, our verdict standard_physics), making the cohort TWELVE; update the tally prose “ten closed windows”->“twelve” and “seven standard_physics/recycled”->“nine”, and “nine closed windows” (the excl-073 figure)->“eleven.” This strengthens the argument (longer silence, larger N). Alternative if a narrower scope is intended: replace “every prediction whose window has closed with no dome-posted result” with an explicit scope (e.g. “every prediction in the 2026-04-30 closure batch plus subsequent closures”) and reconcile the cherry-picking rebuttal accordingly, noting 072/084 are covered in 6.12. Also consider flipping 072/084 author_status pending->dome_silent_terminal in predictions.json for consistency with the standardization rule (both are >14d past close).

holes_found.description: TABLE COLUMN MISLABEL. The cohort table column header reads “Dome status” and displays values like “dome_silent_terminal · 39d silent” for the eight 2026-04-30 entries. But per the sections own “Author-status standardization” block, dome_silent_terminal is OUR review-assigned reconstruction (the dome itself leaves these as pending). A reader who skims the table — and TLDR/table is what most readers see — will read “Dome status: dome_silent_terminal” as a status the DOME declared, when in fact the dome declared nothing (that silence is the whole point). The disclosure exists only later in body prose.
holes_found.recommendation: Rename the column to “Status (author-side, reconstructed)” or add an inline “(reconstructed)” marker on the eight standardized rows; keep PRED-073/105 distinguishable since 105 was already terminal. This removes the skim-level misread without weakening the argument.

holes_found.description: PROVENANCE OF THE “ZERO DOME-POSTED RESULTS” CLAIM. “Zero dome-posted results” is the load-bearing empirical assertion. In predictions.json only PRED-073 (“silent_ignore confirmed 2026-06-05”) and PRED-105 carry an explicit poller/live-site confirmation that the dome posted nothing. The eight 2026-04-30 entries assert dome silence without an inline confirmation date, so a defender can charge that the “zero” is inferred from our own stale catalog rather than a check of the dome’s live predictions page. CLAUDE.md discipline requires reasoning from the dome’s published surface.
holes_found.recommendation: Add a one-line provenance note to the section (or per-row) citing the date the dome predictions page was last checked and found to carry no result for these IDs (mirror the PRED-073 “confirmed 2026-06-05” pattern). Mechanically cheap; closes the inference-vs-observation gap.

holes_found.description: INTERPRETED WINDOW DATES PRESENTED AS PRECISE. Some close dates are our interpretation of vague dome windows: PRED-106’s note says window “April 2026” was “interpreted as closing 2026-04-30 EOM”; PRED-072/084 windows are “April 4-11.” The table shows crisp dates with no marker that some are interpretive. Low risk because the interpretation is reasonable, but a defender could nitpick the silence-clock start.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional: footnote that windows stated as a month are scored as closing at month-end. Not blocking.

holes_found.description: SILENCE COUNTS ARE A FIXED SNAPSHOT. 39/51/8-day counts are as-of integration (2026-06-08); they read like live values but will drift (today is 2026-06-09). Cosmetic.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional: prefix “as of <date>” so the numbers don’t read as auto-updating.

stronger_arguments.description: Quantify the asymmetry directly: state the dome’s confirmed-win count delta over the same 2026-04 to 2026-06 window alongside the 0/12 posted-result count for closed-but-unconfirmed predictions. “Win column +N, loss column +0 over the identical period” makes the one-directional-scoreboard claim concrete rather than rhetorical.

Adding PRED-072/084 lets the section note the silence is LONGER for the overlooked pair (58d vs 39d), turning the fix into a strengthening: the dome’s oldest closed-no-result predictions are the most silent, the opposite of “data not in yet.”

kernel_of_truth.description: The section is analytically sound and unusually honest. Every per-prediction verdict matches data/predictions.json on independent check (data/predictions.json:PRED-087 through PRED-073), the CHAOS citation scaffolding verifies (Finlay et al. 2020, Earth Planets Space 72:156, DOI 10.1186/s40623-020-01252-9 confirmed; CHAOS-8 is valid 1999-2025 and genuinely does not cover April-May 2026, DOI 10.1186/s40623-025-02352-0), and the PRED-073 “falsified on the dome’s own rule under the consensus null, not by a fresh measurement” caveat (data/predictions.json:PRED-073) is exactly the kind of self-limiting honesty that makes the section credible. The author-status standardization’s choice to reuse dome_silent_terminal rather than coin a fourth silence label avoids taxonomy bloat (EXP-606.json author_status_standardization).
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: None of this is in question — the section’s thesis (asymmetric accounting) holds. The single defect is that the section’s OWN completeness/anti-cherry-picking claim (“defined mechanically — every prediction whose window has closed”, data/sections.json:p6-615-silent-ignore-cohort) is contradicted by two omitted PRED-class entries already in our 6.12 list (data/predictions.json:PRED-072, data/predictions.json:PRED-084). The argument survives the fix; it is just not yet airtight on the one axis where the dome can hit back hardest.

deeper_analysis: Verification chain: (1) p6-615 integrated into sections.json after p6-614-kappa-cluster — confirmed. (2) All 10 cohort our_verdict + 8 author_status flips reproduce against predictions.json — confirmed. (3) Dates/silence arithmetic reproduce as-of 2026-06-08 — confirmed. (4) Citations: Finlay 2020 CHAOS-7 and CHAOS-8 (1999-2025) both verified live — confirmed; phantom WIN-071 confirmed absent from wins.json (max id 070), WIN-066 present so PRED-090 recycle is valid. (5) Cohort completeness: FAILED — 14 closed-no-result entries in predictions.json, cohort lists 10; PRED-072 and PRED-084 (PRED-class, closed 2026-04-11, pending, standard_physics, both in our 6.12 eleven) are omitted while nine of 6.12’s eleven are re-listed, making the “every prediction” defense false. This is the one decider-actionable hole. MT-003 (manual_test, predates registration) and PROS-003 (prospective, FAIL-008) are defensibly excluded. Net: ship after H1 fix; H2/H3 are cheap hardening of a section that will be quoted back at us specifically because it accuses the dome of selective bookkeeping.

summary_for_decider: Section 6.15 is analytically sound and the data all checks out, but it has ONE major self-inflicted hole (H1): it claims the silent-ignore cohort is “defined mechanically — every prediction whose window has closed with no dome-posted result,” yet omits PRED-072 and PRED-084 — two PRED-class closed-window/pending entries already in our own 6.12 eleven-closure list. The fix is small and strengthening: add them as two rows (close 2026-04-11, 58d silent, standard_physics), bump tally “ten”->“twelve” and “seven”->“nine,” and (optionally) flip their predictions.json author_status to dome_silent_terminal. Because this section’s thesis IS “the dome accounts selectively,” an incomplete cohort here is a credibility liability; prioritize H1. H2 (table column “Dome status” shows our reconstructed values) and H3 (“zero posted results” lacks inline live-site confirmation provenance for the 8 Apr-30 entries) are cheap moderate hardenings. No verdict change; current argument holds.
